name: Same Budget, Two Outcomes
why_it_works: When the money is held equal, the only variable left is the decision, so the viewer has nothing to blame but the approach. That makes the lesson feel fair, and it positions {{brand}} as the smarter way to spend a budget the viewer already has.

hook.pattern: Fix the budget at one exact number, then split the screen into two ways of spending it.
examples: {{budget}}, spent two ways. Only one built anything.
Same {{budget}}. Same month. Completely different results.
Where your {{budget}} goes decides whether anyone remembers it.

variables.name: scattered_way
variables.description: The common, scattered way to spend it
variables.example: random boosted posts and a cheap logo pack

variables.name: focused_way
variables.example: one game-day shoot that fed a month of posts

variables.name: result_line
variables.description: Honest description of the difference, no invented metrics
variables.example: 30 usable clips vs 4 posts nobody saved

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of a neat stack of cash split down the middle by a strip of tape on a dark table, one half lit cool blue, the other warm gold, top-down, crisp detail
Vertical collage-style photo of a phone screen with scattered unrelated posts, low engagement, cluttered overlapping frames, cool flat light, slightly chaotic composition
Vertical behind-the-scenes shot of a small crew filming {{focused_way}}, camera gimbal moving smoothly, stadium or studio lights, energetic but controlled, cinematic color
Vertical split image, top a sparse feed with a few mismatched posts, bottom a consistent polished content grid in matching {{brand}} style, clean even light

craft.notes: Say the exact budget number in the first two seconds and repeat it once on screen; a specific number reads as real. Keep the two sides parallel in length and framing so the only thing that differs is the decision.

do_not: Invent follower counts, revenue or view numbers; describe output you actually delivered
Shame people who boosted posts; most viewers have done it
Use a real team's or athlete's footage without rights
